headline: 《遺忘之島》動畫評價兩極
context: 夢工廠（DreamWorks）新片《Forgotten Island》，講的是菲律賓兩位好友，意外發現一道通往奇幻生物世界的傳送門，卻得想辦法回家的故事。有評論形容，這是一部「菲律賓風味的超自然冒險片」；但也有評論批評，整部片步調過於緊繃急促，角色幾乎沒有喘息、被賦予深度的空間。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: This over-controlled adventure never takes a breath or a moment to let its characters come to life Frantically and even stroboscopically over-energised, this big new movie from DreamWorks about best friends for ever seems to me another example of exhausting AI-type content production in animation. You could make the same argument against plenty of live-action films of course, but it is in animation that this kind of soulless blitzkrieg tends to predominate. Forgotten Island is over-controlled and over-determined, a movie that never, or hardly ever, takes its pedal from the metal, never takes a breath or a moment to let its characters come to life. At times it seems to be aping the world of Japanese anime, but without its sense of character or capacity for calm. The story, weirdly reminiscent of The Hangover of all things, is set in the Philippines in the pre-social media 90s. Jo, voiced by R&B star HER, is a lonely and super-imaginative teen always in trouble at school; like Moana she has a wise grandma who guides her to her ancestral destiny and has captivated Jo with stories of her culture and identity – stories of the forgotten island of Nakali. Jo makes friends with similarly lonely Raissa (Liza Soberano) who like Jo is smart but with a much more focused sense of academic discipline. Continue reading...

voice_text: 夢工廠出了一部新的動畫片，片名《Forgotten Island》。故事講的是菲律賓兩位好朋友，意外發現一道通往奇幻生物世界的傳送門，接下來得想辦法回家。有評論形容，這是一部菲律賓風味的超自然冒險片；但也有評論批評，整部片步調過於緊繃急促，角色幾乎沒有喘息、被賦予深度的空間。
